records.title: NLL-Guided Full-Attention Layer Selection for Training-Free Sliding-Window Adaptation
records.reason: The paper targets long-context LLM inference efficiency. It calibrates each layer's contribution to answer-token prediction by measuring the NLL change when that layer uses full attention rather than sliding-window attention during prefill, then keeps only the top-k layers full-attention while retaining full-attention decode. This directly addresses prefill compute and accuracy tradeoffs in hybrid attention deployment, so it is in scope for inference/serving.
records.body_check: Read the primary arXiv v1 HTML body: §1 and §2 for the long-context inference motivation and distinction from KV compression/other hybrid-attention work; §3.1–§3.4 for the budgeted layer-selection objective, answer-token teacher-forced NLL scoring, top-k selection, and calibration/inference procedure; §4.1–§4.6, Table 1, Table 2, and Figures 2–3 for setup, results, per-task and de-confounding analysis, selection stability; §5 and Appendix A.4 for limitations and uncertainty. On Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and LongMemEval (500 examples, ~24k-token prompts), with 2048-token SWA window, keep-first=10, full-attention decode, 9/36 selected layers score 64.6%, versus 54.2% for the periodic 1/4-FA baseline and 65.0% for periodic 1/2-FA; reported 95% binomial half-widths are about 4 percentage points. Calibration uses 64 LongAlign-10k/fusang-v1-filtered examples and about 15 minutes on 4 GPUs; the authors estimate break-even after ~1,354 inference requests at 24k prompt length. Limitations: one model and one benchmark; authors call for cross-model/task validation, cross-domain calibration analysis, paired bootstrap/judge-replication statistics, and additional FA budgets. Sixteen calibration examples yield 62.2% and 0.64 Jaccard overlap with the 64-example selection. The paper discloses that FARS autonomously produced the work and that the prose is primarily machine-generated; treat the reported experimental claims as author-reported. The paper states accompanying code is public (GitLab URL in the primary HTML).

records.title: ProtoKV: Streaming Video Understanding under Delayed Query with Summary-State Memory
records.reason: ProtoKVは、ストリーミング動画を扱うvision-language modelのKV memoryを一定容量に保ち、遅れて届く質問に対する推論を支援する方式である。近傍履歴は正確なKVのまま保持し、古い履歴はtoken instanceの保持・追い出しに依存せず、空間・時間情報を用いたprototype bankと残差統計へオンライン集約する。質問時には各prototypeを少数のpseudo-KV tokenとして合成し、mass-aware biasとともに通常のattentionへ渡す。固定memory budget下で、長い遅延のあるstreaming video understandingを評価し、特にfar historyに依存する領域でKV token retentionやsliding-window baselineより精度低下を抑える。これは既存H2Oが扱うKV cacheの選択・圧縮とは対象モデルと動画ストリーミングの遅延queryという設定を異にするが、LLM/VLM推論時のKV memory管理を直接研究し、同じKV cache最適化の系統に位置付くためacceptとする。根拠と限界: arXiv本文§3はnear window、continuity-awareなprototype assignment、残差統計、pseudo-token interfaceを説明し、§4.2–4.4は二つの7B vision-language backboneと四つのSVU benchmarkでmatched memory budgetの比較・ablationを報告する。最大遅延ではRVS-MovieでSWA比+20.4ポイント、token-retention比+12.5ポイントを報告する一方、精度は遅延増加に伴い全方式で下がる。評価上の制約として、benchmarkに各queryの実際のevidence timestampがないためdatasetのquery timestampを遅延のproxyに用い、query shiftで正解が変わらないretrospective queryだけを同一intersection subset上で評価している。加えてonline updateはQwen2.5-VL-7B/RTX 5090/RVS-Egoで33.8 ms/frame（per-frame processingの約30.8%）と計測され、query時のTTFTに直接加算されない説明だがstream ingestionのコストは残る。著者らは反復する視覚的に類似した事象の分離・計数ではprototype capacityが境界をぼかす弱点も報告する。従って効果の主張は報告されたSVU benchmark・backbone・budgetの範囲に限り、実環境の一般性能とは扱わない。
records.body_check: arXivの一次本文 (https://arxiv.org/html/2606.26762) を確認: §2.3 query delayの定義とbenchmark上のproxy、§3 ProtoKV、§4.1–4.7 実験・遅延robustness・ablation・system validation、§6 Conclusion、Appendix C.1 query selectionとC.3 online update overhead、Appendix D.2 task-type breakdown。§3ではexact near-window KVと固定容量far prototype bank、continuity-aware assignment、product-quantization由来残差統計、pseudo-KV synthesis、mass biasを確認。§4.2 Table 1ではLLaVA-OV-7BとQwen2.5-VL-7BでRVS-Ego/RVS-Movie/OVO-Bench/StreamingBenchを比較し、§4.3は最大遅延でRVS-MovieのSWA比+20.4pp、token-retention比+12.5ppを記載。§4.4 Table 2のLLaVA-OV-7B/RVS-EgoではΔ=30のfull ProtoKVが54.3%、near-onlyが40.5%、far-onlyが49.2%。§4.7 Table 4はLLaVA-OV-7B/RVS-EgoでProtoKVがReKVに対し同じ23.0 GB peak GPU memory、accuracy 58.0%対58.8%、TTFT 1.06秒対1.43秒、E2E 2.90秒対3.92秒と報告。§4.7/Appendix C.3は別設定Qwen2.5-VL-7B・RTX 5090・RVS-Egoでupdate overhead 33.8ms/frame、total per-frame processing timeの30.8%と報告。Appendix C.1は実evidence時刻を含むannotationがないためdataset query timestampをproxyとし、時間シフトに不変のretrospective queryを選び、すべてのdelay値に有効な共通subsetで比較することを明記。Appendix D.2では似た反復事象のcountingに弱いと分析。arXiv abstractはtitle、著者、arXiv ID、submitted dateをworklistと照合。

records.title: Speculation at a Distance: Where Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding Actually Pays Off
records.reason: This paper analyzes distributed speculative decoding for LLM inference/serving across edge devices and cloud servers, directly within the survey's inference and serving scope. It compares synchronous and pipelined distributed speculative decoding with co-located speculative decoding and cloud autoregressive decoding, derives bounded latency conditions, and identifies multi-tenant server capacity as the strongest case for offloading draft compute. The paper's capacity result depends on cross-client overlap; its per-request analysis assumes fixed, contention-free service times. It is an analytical study supported by cited measurements from prior systems, not a new end-to-end experimental evaluation.
records.body_check: Read arXiv HTML v2 (https://arxiv.org/html/2606.25091v2): Abstract; §I Introduction and Table I; §II-A Co-located SD, §II-B DSD (synchronous), §II-C DSD (pipelined); §III-A comparison with co-located SD and Proposition 1; §III-B cloud-AR latency bound (Proposition 2, Table IV), compute/memory/API feasibility; §III-C multi-tenant server capacity (Proposition 8 and Remarks 9-11); §IV pipelining condition (Proposition 12) and cited system measurements; §V Conclusion. Main findings: synchronous DSD adds network latency/communication vs co-located SD; cloud-AR latency gains exist only under a bounded RTT/acceptance/model-speed window; pipelining beats co-located SD only if RTT plus transfer fits within the edge drafting window and speculative waste is small; offloading may raise concurrent-client capacity under sufficient cross-client overlap. Limits: fixed contention-free per-request times, a constant conditional acceptance model, low-transfer-overhead simplification in numerical examples, illustrative rather than direct 4G/cross-region operating points, and capacity gains that depend on overlap and verification remaining memory-bound. Cited experiments are prior work and do not validate a universal capacity factor.
